directive.thread_id: film repository port 2026-11-05, lane film-tools: the narrator tools of a film
directive.quote: Finish the port of the film repository so it can be retired: move each job to its correct home, porting the correct parts one to one and never rebuilding from scratch what already worked; move the code byte for byte, then make what it fixed arguments and settings.

targets.baseline_commit_message: fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words: a film's hand-written token table and slot-variant writer, moved byte for byte

preserve: one variant per candidate with every other slot at its base pick, the base first
each variant writes lines/<id>.txt, shots/<id>.json and claims/<id>.json with one claim entry per sentence
lines.txt and manifest.json in the order of the variants
allowed_deltas: the folders it wrote from where it sat are out.here (lines, lines.txt, manifest) and out.narrator (shots, claims)

the slots, candidates, sentences, ids and about texts are the person's settings row; its sentences() and claim_for() rules for one line (lines 62-96) are sentence templates with claim_from in that row, and variants() is picks_of() over the row's slots
one JSON answer as the last line after the old count line; refusals say what to change
banned_substitutions: a person's words or slot tables written into the code
_paths: The source lives in a private repository, so it is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash); a checkout of that repository beside this one finds it. Lines holding a person's name or a private path are left out of the sources (each source names its lines), so they never reach this public repository; the first source is the byte copy. The source is the write loop of main() (lines 99-123, without the lines holding a private name); lines 62-96 encoded one film's sentence and candidate tables, which are now the person's settings row.
